Unique key for the responsible party information stored in tblMpPaymentResponsibleParty  If the payment has a responsible party and a payment is reversed using the fblnPostNewDebt option on the reversal reason, the reversed payment liability will be posted to the responsible party account. This should only be used if a third party is responsible if a payment is reversed.  Examples of a responsible party are: DSVS  If a dealerships pays for a vehicle registration and then bounces the check, the dealership would be liable for the non-sufficient funds and not the individual vehicle owners that the payment had offset. In this instance, the dealership accountkey should be set as the responsible party account key so the system knows where to apply the NSF.  Tax If a trustee makes a payment to multiple accounts and the trustee bounces the check and the business process specifies that the trustee owes the money and not the accounts that were paid, then the trustee would be the responsible party for the payment.   Examples of situations that are not responsible parties. If making a payment on an account and the account would be liable for the dishonored check, then the responsible party key should not be set. The default is to post the NSF liability to the account of the allocation and setting a responsible party would cause the payment to "Stick" to the original account if the payment was transferred.

Customers are linked when two customers jointly file and owe a single debt.  This convention is most commonly used for Individual Income Tax when a taxpayer and a spouse are jointly liable for a single debt for which they filed jointly.  The link between the two is established by way of core business object calls that are triggered either by manual user action that explicitly establishes the link or configurable automated actions (e.g. during returns processing).  The system maintains financial activity for joint accounts on the Prime account (flngAccountKey) which belongs to the Prime customer (flngCustomerKey).  No financials information will be associated with the Joint account (flngJointAccountKey) that belongs to the Joint customer (flngJointCustomerKey) for the joint filing periods.
This is used primarily for Individual Income Tax, in which you have joint filers. This would generally be the account key of the joint account (e.g., spouse).  See flngJointCustomerKey.

This is used primarily for Individual Income Tax, in which you have joint filers. This flag is used to indicate which account in a joint filing situation is the Prime account. If this flag is True, then the account is the prime filer and the flngJointAccountKey associated would be the joint filer. If False, then the customer is the joint filer and the flngJointAccountKey account is the prime.  The system maintains financial information only on the Prime account for joint periods.

Unique key for the responsible party information stored in tblMpPaymentResponsibleParty  If the payment has a responsible party and a payment is reversed using the fblnPostNewDebt option on the reversal reason, the reversed payment liability will be posted to the responsible party account. This should only be used if a third party is responsible if a payment is reversed.  Examples of a responsible party are: DSVS  If a dealerships pays for a vehicle registration and then bounces the check, the dealership would be liable for the non-sufficient funds and not the individual vehicle owners that the payment had offset. In this instance, the dealership accountkey should be set as the responsible party account key so the system knows where to apply the NSF.  Tax If a trustee makes a payment to multiple accounts and the trustee bounces the check and the business process specifies that the trustee owes the money and not the accounts that were paid, then the trustee would be the responsible party for the payment.   Examples of situations that are not responsible parties. If making a payment on an account and the account would be liable for the dishonored check, then the responsible party key should not be set. The default is to post the NSF liability to the account of the allocation and setting a responsible party would cause the payment to "Stick" to the original account if the payment was transferred.
